findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical answer-space binary search with a greedy minimum-group feasibility scan. Its scalar state is concise, conventional, and directly tied to the monotone predicate, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 410 and its Python splitArray surface. The Reference preserves exactly-k non-empty contiguous splitting, the minimax objective, both explained source examples, the subarray definition, and all three source constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064734753. Its lower and upper bounds, midpoint feasibility scan, greedy cut rule, group-count comparison, and lower-bound convergence are exactly the protected app-local algorithm apart from the LeetCode wrapper and annotation.

The legal 32-, 96-, and 256-element unit-array tiers span 8x with k fixed at two and force complete scans. The current source passes all 11 executions at -0.02 relative growth and 0.97x; correct partition dynamic programming passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.94 and 45.63x.

The Approach derives the tight answer bounds, proves the nonnegative greedy scan minimizes group count, explains conversion from at most k to exactly k groups, and proves monotonic convergence. It now defines S precisely as the count of integer candidate limits and states O(n log S) time with O(1) space.
The hash-bound public Reference retains the complete minimax split contract, both source examples and explanations in order, all three constraints, and the absence of source visuals or tables.
